summary.prose: This Story lets a JetBrains user set a tier to the Claude tool on an Ollama model from insrc's Settings. The runner already appears in the Model Tiers runner list because it lists every family the daemon declares; this Story marks each of its models cloud or local in the model list, keeps it out of the Check model dialog, and shows a configured model it does not declare as 'not supported, the tier will not run' instead of saying the daemon runs a default. The family is recognised by the definitions' host mark, never by name.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Model the new runner as a new family in the model definitions (alternative a1). The definitions file, its validator and the definitions answer gain one family, 'ollama-claude', with the CLI kind 'claude' and a host mark 'ollama'; every model of that family carries a hosting mark, 'cloud' or 'local'. Tier settings, effort filtering and provider construction keep their one per-family path. A family with the Ollama host mark builds the existing CLI provider with an Ollama target applied to that subprocess only, and clients use the host mark to show cloud/local and to never offer unlisted model ids for that family. Scope change 2026-10-29 (user decision): the Codex-on-Ollama family is withdrawn, because Ollama's cloud models ignore a requested output format and the Codex tool depends on it (DEF non-goal, citation c9 of the DEF).

consumedContracts.name: Ollama-hosted CLI families in the definitions answer
consumedContracts.purpose: The wire shape every consumer reads to know the new family, that it runs a CLI on Ollama, and which of its models are cloud or local.

consumedContracts.name: Tier resolution on an Ollama-hosted family
consumedContracts.purpose: How the daemon reports the tier it actually runs when the tier names a host family, including a model the definitions do not declare, so the run layer and every settings surface show the same outcome.

boundary.internal: The JetBrains Settings page's family and model selectors, the cloud/local labels, the filter that keeps host families out of the model-check flow, and its display of the resolved tier stay inside s5.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The shipped definitions entry for the new family and its models (which cloud and local models are supported), the catalog validator's four-member check and the 'hosting required on host families' rule, the registry's mapping from a CLI client to its direct family only, and the refusal of the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families stay inside s1.

How the CLI provider points a run at Ollama (the claude environment, applied only to that subprocess), the pre-run checks that Ollama answers and the model is available or signed in for a cloud model, the failure messages that name the cause, and the time limit that keeps a run from waiting forever stay inside s2.
The terminal UI's runner list, model list with cloud/local labels, effort step and the withheld 'enter another id' path for host families, and its display of the resolved tier, stay inside s3.

The VS Code tier picker's family and model steps, the settings write validation that refuses an undeclared model for a host family, the cloud/local labels and the withheld 'enter another id' item stay inside s4.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — run on Ollama and expose in settings

nonFunctional.performance: No added cost on today's runners. A run on a host family adds one Ollama reachability and model-availability check before the CLI starts; a run never waits beyond the existing CLI time limit.
nonFunctional.security: The Ollama settings are applied only to the started subprocess's environment or arguments; the user's own CLI configuration files and the daemon's environment are never changed. No API key is stored; the claude CLI gets the placeholder token Ollama accepts locally.
nonFunctional.observability: The daemon logs the family, model, hosting and Ollama target of each host-family run, and a failed pre-run check logs which check failed; the tier resolution reported to clients names a 'model-not-supported' fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Nothing new is persisted: tier settings keep their stored shape, and the new families live in the shipped definitions file.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Parses host on a family and hosting on a model from models.definitions; recognises the host family by host, never by id.

Mirrors the daemon's resolution for a host family on the Settings page: a declared model runs as configured (an effort it does not take is shown dropped); an undeclared one is noted as not supported, the tier will not run.

errorCases.scenario: The tier is configured (hand-edited config, or a model removed later) on the Claude-on-Ollama runner with a model it does not declare, and the Settings page opens.
errorCases.detection: resolve() finds the configured family has a host and served(family, model) returns null.
errorCases.response: The tier row's note reads '<model> is not supported by <displayName> — the tier will not run'; the model combo shows the non-selectable '(current, not supported): <id>' marker above the declared models; unsavable() refuses to save an edit still on that model ('choose a listed model for the <tier> tier first').
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees the tier does not run (the daemon's model-not-supported refusal) and picks a listed model; nothing undeclared is written.

errorCases.scenario: The user opens Check model… to try an unlisted id for the Claude-on-Ollama runner.
errorCases.detection: ModelCheckFlow.families() filters out families whose host is set.
errorCases.response: The dialog's family list offers only vendor CLI families; the host family is not there.
errorCases.userImpact: No check the daemon would refuse is offered; the runner accepts only its listed models.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is down or an older daemon answers the definitions without host or hosting.
errorCases.detection: gateway.modelDefinitions() fails (existing ModelDefinitionsResult.Failed path), or parseModelDefinitions finds no host / hosting keys.
errorCases.response: Daemon down: the existing failure message and hidden rows until Refresh. No host field: host and hosting are null, so the family behaves as today's CLI families (no marks, offered in Check model, the 'runs its default' note).
errorCases.userImpact: No new failure mode; labels and the not-supported note appear once the daemon is s1 or later.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Every runner, model and effort the Settings page offers comes from the daemon's models.definitions answer; the plugin keeps no family or model list and names no family id.
Writes are one whole tier {runner, model, effort} per dirty, savable tier; an unlisted model is never written (unsavable).
Vendor CLI families stay in Check model… and keep the 'not listed — the daemon runs its default' note; plain Ollama is unchanged.
The DTOs stay structural mirrors of the daemon's answer: a malformed family or model is skipped, and an answer without the new keys parses unchanged.

migration.stateBefore: The JetBrains Model Tiers settings (jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/settings/ModelTiersModel.kt over daemon/ModelDefinitions.kt) already list every family the definitions declare, including the Claude-on-Ollama one, but the DTOs drop host and hosting, so models carry no cloud/local mark, an undeclared host-family model is noted as 'the daemon runs its default for the tier instead' (wrong: nothing runs), and settings/ModelCheckFlow.kt offers the host family in Check model…, whose check the daemon refuses.
migration.stateAfter: The plugin parses host and hosting: the model combo labels a host family's models cloud or local, an undeclared host-family model is noted 'not supported — the tier will not run' with a '(current, not supported)' marker, and Check model… offers only vendor CLI families. Vendor and plain Ollama behaviour is unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add nullable host to the family DTO and nullable hosting to the model DTO, and read them in the definitions parser.
Show the hosting in the model combo label and the not-supported note and marker for a host family in the tier model.
Exclude families with a host from the Check model flow's family list.

migration.backwardCompat: Plugin-internal change: the new DTO fields default to null, nothing persisted changes, tier writes keep their whole-tier shape, and an older daemon's answer (no host/hosting) renders as today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-aware DTOs, tier model and check-flow filter over the definitions answer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parse host/hosting into the plugin's DTOs; ModelTiersModel labels a host family's models cloud/local and reports an undeclared host-family model as not supported (the tier will not run); ModelCheckFlow keeps host families out of Check model.
alternativesConsidered.approach: daemon/ModelDefinitions.kt: DefinedFamilyDto gains `host: String?` and DefinedModelDto gains `hosting: String?`, read by parseModelDefinitions (absent on an older daemon, so null). settings/ModelTiersModel.kt: label() appends ' — cloud' / ' — local' from hosting; resolve() notes, for a configured model a host family does not declare, '<model> is not supported by <family> — the tier will not run' instead of 'the daemon runs its default for the tier instead'; the non-selectable current marker reads '(current, not supported): <id>' for a host family (ModelChoice.CurrentNotInCatalog gains the label choice). runnerOptions already lists every family with models (ac1); effortOptions already offers only '' plus the model's own efforts (ac2); unsavable/collectWrites already refuse to write an unlisted model and write whole tiers; resolve/onSaved already report the saved tier on reopen (ac3). settings/ModelCheckFlow.kt: families() returns families with a cliKind and no host, so the Check model… dialog never offers the host family. The family is recognised by host, never by id.
pros: Smallest change: three Kotlin files plus tests, reusing the headless model, its tests and the existing gate bridge.
Same rule as the daemon (s1), the TUI (s3) and VS Code (s4), keyed on the host mark.
No daemon or IPC change; older daemons behave as today.
cons: The model mirrors the daemon's tier resolution rather than asking for it, as it already does for vendor families.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask the daemon for each tier's resolution
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a per-tier resolution request to the daemon and render the Settings page's current tier and notes from it, plus a1's labels and check-flow filter.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new daemon IPC returning resolveTierWith's TierResolution for core/mid/cheap (including fallback 'model-not-supported'); DaemonGateway gains a call for it; ModelTiersModel takes the resolution instead of computing resolve() itself. The cloud/local labels and the Check model filter still need a1's DTO fields.
pros: The displayed tier is exactly what the daemon computes.
cons: A new daemon IPC outside s5's boundary (s1 owns sc2), so an HLD amendment, and every client would be expected to adopt it.
Still needs all of a1's changes; one more request and a new older-daemon failure mode.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same on ac1-ac3 but partial on sc2 and k4 (new IPC outside s5's boundary) and strictly more work, since it still needs a1's changes.
